description:
List the orders created in this session, each with its live status.

Scoped to this session's own Order Records: an order placed
in another session, or by another caller, is not listed here — it is
reached through `order_lookup` with the customer's reference + email.
Whenever you tell the customer that only this conversation's orders can be
shown, also tell them they can see any other order of theirs by giving its
order reference and the email they used at checkout.
`last` is false when the session has more orders than one call shows
(only the most recent are returned); `total_elements` is the session's
true order count, so a false `last` means older orders exist beyond the
list.

Returns a job — poll until SUCCEEDED. On failure the job error is
`RendrealNotConfiguredError` (no client) or a `Rendreal*Error` — the
latter only when every listed order's status read fails (a systemic
outage); one failed read degrades that row to a null status and the job
still succeeds. An order deleted upstream is omitted from the list
entirely (and from `total_elements`), never shown as a pickable row.

The widget's picker commits an ordinal reference with the order's status
attached for disambiguation (e.g. "Nr 2 - Complete, please.") rather
than an id — 1-indexed against this same call's `orders` list, in
order. Map the number back to that list position's `order_id` before
calling `order_get` (these are this session's own orders, so no email is
needed); don't match on status alone (several orders can share one).
name: order_list

anyOf.description:
The Runner's response to a `@runner.job` invocation.

On the fast path (work completed within budget), `status` is SUCCEEDED
or FAILED and `result` / `error` is populated. On the slow path,
`status` is RUNNING and `job_id` is the handle the host LLM uses for
`poll()`.

On FAILED, `error` is the safe class-name code; `reason` / `detail` are
populated only when the failure carries a host-safe explanation (e.g. a
RendReal rejection's server message + body), else they stay None.

On RUNNING, `note` carries model-facing guidance: it tells the host LLM whether
a widget is already polling the job, or whether it must call `poll_job` itself.

Canonical short-circuit response shape.

`status` is always `"error"` — acts as a discriminator for LLM consumers.
`error` is a machine-readable code (e.g. `session_not_found`).
`reason` is a human-readable explanation of why the call failed.
`detail` carries structured extra context (ids, available values, etc.).

title: List this session's orders
